absent: Locking, reference counting and RCU or SRCU protection rules for live tracepoint registration and uprobe management are not shown.
Enabled-mode tracepoint emission, callback invocation order and return values are not shown.
Enabled-mode uprobe insertion, breakpoint handling, single-step emulation and return-probe chaining behavior are not shown.
BPF runner implementations, perf permission checks and trace flag effects are not shown.
Remote event identifier allocation, transport and consumption are not shown.
Power, printk, module, DMA, debug and audit behaviors outside tracing and uprobes are not shown in these fragments.

findings.text: Without tracepoint support one declaration yields a closed family of helpers sharing the event name covering emission, direct invocation, probe registration, probe unregistration, callback signature checking, and two enabled tests.

In the disabled configuration registration helpers report unavailability, emission and checking helpers have no observable effect, enabled tests report disabled, and definition plus export macros expand to nothing with no object or symbol created.

Public declaration macros normalize caller prototype and argument lists, suffix plain names, require the current processor to be online, optionally conjoin a caller predicate, and prepend an opaque data pointer to the probe prototype before delegating to a common internal declaration for regular, conditional, syscall and event forms.

When the tracing backend is absent, class declaration does nothing while concrete event macros discard layout, assignment and formatting material and reduce to matching plain or conditional trace declarations; no-operation variants provide only a silent emission helper plus disabled predicate, or nothing for class forms.

The literal-string helper has two modes: one pins the supplied pointer in a dedicated retained section and evaluates to the saved pointer, the other is an identity returning its input unchanged with no section attribute.

A uprobe consumer record carries an entry callback, an optional return callback, an optional address-space filter, list linkage for co-located consumers, and a numeric identity assigned at registration; entry observation includes registers and a data word while return observation additionally includes the probed function address.
Handler dispositions are removal one and ignore two; maximum nested return-probe depth is sixty four; the sentinel meaning no trampoline address is an all-ones unsigned long.

A per-task uprobe execution marker distinguishes running, single-step requested, single-step acknowledged, and single-step trapped, separating normal execution from phases of emulating an intercepted instruction.

A return-probe handle distinguishes leased under read-side protection, stable under reference count, gone when neither protection holds, and consumed after its handler ran; a separate discriminator distinguishes plain call, chained call, and return interception sites.
A lightweight return-probe handle stores its lifecycle state, a per-processor read-side counter used while leased, and a pointer to the underlying probe object.

Per-task uprobe state records the execution marker, return-probe nesting depth and stack, a pool plus timer and sequence counter for return instances, either architecture execution context with fault address or deferred copy work with its address, the active probe and its out-of-line address, a signal-suppression flag, and an architecture probe pointer.

A return interception record holds its handle, probed function and stack addresses, saved return address, nesting and consumer-count metadata, intrusive stack linkage with deferred reclamation, one inline consumer slot plus an optional overflow array for further consumers, and cache-line alignment; each consumer slot pairs a cookie with a consumer identity.

Process-wide uprobe state is either a single pointer to an out-of-line execution area when enabled, or an empty record when disabled; disabled mode also defines initialization as empty and trap address as the current instruction pointer.

Without uprobe support the management and lifecycle operations are inert shims: creation reports an encoded unavailability failure, state change reports unavailability, unregistration and address-space notifications do nothing, mapping reports success, duplication and resume handling do nothing, signal denial reports false, and task copy plus state clearing do nothing.

BPF trace glue maps argument sizes of one, two, four or eight to the matching unsigned integer width, copies the argument representation into that width, and widens the result to sixty four bits, with automatic selection among one to twelve argument expansions.

For each trace class or trace declaration the BPF layer emits a non-traced trampoline forwarding normalized arguments to the matching arity-specific runner, plus a retained map entry in a dedicated section binding the kernel tracepoint object to that trampoline together with argument count and writable size, and a compile-time type compatibility probe.

Writable event variants statically require the declared writable size to equal the size of the object behind the first argument; syscall trace variants additionally mark the trampoline as potentially faulting before dispatch.
Two small perf helpers return their count and task inputs unchanged.

Remote event support defines field descriptors from type, name, size, alignment and signedness, selects among zero, one or two argument print helpers, prints the event name followed by formatted payload, and registers a section-placed descriptor carrying name, numeric identity, field table, format string and print callback.

The trace definition header redefines the same macro names per inclusion pass: creation passes forward generic, conditional, function-backed and syscall events to corresponding definition primitives with normalized parameters and derive include file and path helpers, while neutral passes empty those declaration macros and only flag multi-read and point creation.

Block tracing reserves ten characters for read-write-sync annotation and names priority classes none, realtime, best-effort, idle and invalid; alarm timer tracing names realtime, boottime and freezer variants; trace subsystems observed here are alarmtimer, avc, block and capability.

A probe handler request to remove the probe from the current process is honored only when the consumer also implements a filter that declines the current address space; without such a filter or when the filter accepts, the removal request has no effect.
Failure-pointer encoding is owned elsewhere; this lane relies on it only as the failure return of disabled probe creation.
